mutants.name: dev-only files entry added to package.json is caught by the leak scan (real mutant tarball)
a zeroed bin/bb fails the installed-binary smoke (real mutant tarball)
wasm registry resolves the vendored xml grammar and rejects bogus names

limitations: The install leg needs network access to the npm registry for runtime deps (native modules download prebuilt binaries or compile); an offline run surfaces as a B-check failure, not a silent pass.
The installed binary is invoked as `node <prefix>/bin/bb` rather than via the npm bin shim; PATH shims are a packaging detail that varies by npm version.
The dev-only-leak regex encodes today's dev directories (script/, validation/, docs/mN/, .github/, ide/, src/); a new top-level dev directory must be added to it.
